hits.draft_en:
Logan Kilpatrick: in the first 72 hours after Gemini 4 Argon launched, Google processed about 25 trillion tokens. 456k views.

Theo replied that T3 Code users processed about 36.5 trillion tokens in the same window. DeepSeek says one of its clusters serves 155 trillion a day.

outsiders.name: Florian Roth ⚡️
outsiders.text:
Since I heard about this #PHP #RCE last week, I've been preparing a tool for everyone who doesn't know what to do right now: 

process-watcher shows you every program your PHP processes start, with full command lines, so you can spot suspicious activity

Until a patch is out, isolation (containers) and tight monitoring are your best bet to limit the damage. And I'm sure the LLMs already go "brrrr" and people are trying to reproduce the vulnerability.

From what I've heard, exploitation will probably show up as suspicious sub process spawns. That's exactly what this watches, using eBPF: one static binary for Linux (amd64, arm64), no dependencies, running in a few minutes. It can also kill the ones you name (dry run first), but it's a detection layer, not a patch, and it can't see anything that happens inside PHP without starting a process.

Quick start: https://t.co/7nluFV3Q25
Project: https://t.co/45agyRKtnS

virals.draft_en:
A critical PHP bug went public today. OpenAI says its models helped find it as part of a coordinated disclosure, and the fix took two months of work across maintainers.

Pieter took all his sites offline until the patch dropped at 2 PM UTC. A friend at a big tech company said he'd patch it in a few days because he's out of office.

If you run anything on PHP, including WordPress:
1. Check your PHP version
2. Update as soon as your host or distro has the fix
3. Treat a firewall rule as a stopgap
4. Make sure someone can patch when you're away

virals.angle: AI finds the bugs, people still have to patch them

Today OpenAI said its models helped researchers find critical flaws in PHP. The same day there were reports of attackers using AI agents against hundreds of banks in Latin America.

The new job isn't finding bugs. It's applying fixes quickly. If you run anything online, set up automatic security updates this week.

virals.angle: Token demand is the real AI story
virals.draft_en:
Three numbers from this week:

Google processed about 25 trillion tokens in Gemini 4 Argon's first 72 hours.
Theo says T3 Code users processed about 36.5 trillion in the same window.
DeepSeek says one cluster serves 155 trillion tokens a day at about $38 revenue per GPU hour.

Whatever you think of the hype, people are using this stuff a lot. If you build on AI, your biggest cost will be usage. Pick models by cost per useful output, not by the leaderboard.

virals_narrative: Window Oct 20 ~11:20 CT (after Tuesday's digest) through Oct 21 ~11:15 CT. The day belonged to a critical PHP vulnerability. Details leaked before a patch, the fix landed at 2 PM UTC (9 AM CT), and OpenAI said its models helped researchers find the flaws in a two-month coordinated effort (1.3M). Pieter took all his sites offline until the patch (276k), then shared a friend at a big tech company who planned to patch 'in a few days' because he was out of office (140k). Around it, the security mood spread: reports of AI agents used against banks, Ethan Mollick on companies drowning in patches, and Nikita Bier wondering if breaches and spam cancel out AI's short-term GDP gains. The biggest watchlist post was lighter: Pieter had Claude Code build a GTA San Andreas mission where CJ vibe codes a startup (762k, 3.7k bookmarks), after finishing his Alexa Jukebox and sharing the full prompt. Logan said Gemini 4 Argon processed about 25 trillion tokens in its first 72 hours (456k), and swyx dug up DeepSeek's claim of 155 trillion tokens a day from one cluster (114k). The meta: be useful on news days (a clear checklist beats a hot take), post the prompt behind your builds, and when someone claims an 'autonomous' business, look for where the audience came from.
